note: Recast from the species-level treatment of Rocha & Cancello (2009), original in English; that treatment carries no measurement table, hence no digital measurements are listed; the type locality, type material and etymology are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is distinguished from the other species of the genus by the combination of large ocelli and the position of the fontanelle relative to the compound eyes; the most similar species is O. wheeleri, from which it differs in the scattered labral setae and the more prominent ocelli that do not touch the compound eye. The soldier has type-2 mandibles and parallel sides of the head in dorsal view, and is larger than O. mirim and O. pilosus; it differs from O. humilis in being smaller, from O. tubesauassu in the wider lateral projections that are not constricted at the base, and from O. wheeleri in lacking an ocellar spot.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes large, separated from the lower margin of the head by less than the greatest diameter of an ocellus. Ocelli semicircular in dorsal view; oval in lateral view and touching the compound eye. Fontanelle wide, of medium size. Head capsule with short hairs, the dorsum with setae. Labral setae arranged in two rows. Pronotum with setae and short hairs, mainly along the margins; mesonotum and metanotum densely setose, concentrated on the centre and the posterior margin. Head brown, pronotum and tergites pale brown, sternites yellow, legs and wing scales pale brown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Sides of the head parallel in dorsal view. Dorsal tubercle prominent in lateral view, situated behind the lateral projection. Mandibles type 2, with a tooth-like process on the proximal half. Head capsule sparsely setose, short hairs denser ventrally, minute hairs scattered over all surfaces. Postmentum with setae and short hairs. The surface of the pronotum with setae and short hairs; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum with short hairs; abdominal tergites and sternites densely covered with short hairs, the posterior margin of the sternites with setae.
